content_of_post_to_comment: A child can take fifteen minutes to walk fifty metres because, from their perspective, they aren’t taking fifteen minutes to get somewhere. The walk itself is what is happening. Adults have divided time into categories: on time and late, useful and wasted. Children have to learn that a puddle can be a delay. That stopping to watch an ant means falling behind. We spend years teaching them our relationship with time. I wonder if we should spend a little more time learning theirs.
comment: Perhaps the challenge isn't teaching children time, but teaching them when urgency is truly necessary. A life organized entirely around schedules can mistake efficiency for meaning.
